note: script_sha256 identifies the code that produced the artifacts; harness_commit is HEAD at generation time and may precede the commit that adds evidence/ to the tree

checks.name: lattice-tests
checks.claim: the vendored lattice's own tests run offline and pass
checks.independence: self-check: asserts literals against the same BAML source; says nothing about the reference implementation

checks.name: lattice-paths
checks.claim: the packed binary and `baml run` are rotations, not variants
checks.independence: packaging check: same BAML source, two execution paths. Rules out a stale or mispacked binary; says nothing about the lattice's meaning

checks.name: lattice-vs-reference
checks.claim: the vendored BAML reproduces the pinned Go reference, including every deviation kind
checks.independence: TRANSCRIPTION, not independence: the BAML was ported from this Go module. Agreement rules out drift; the reference's own tests are the correctness evidence, and they are upstream of this PR

checks.name: byte-safety
checks.claim: the byte gate rejects non-ASCII, control bytes, line-ending damage and oversize programs, and round-trips sha256
checks.independence: self-check: fixtures with known expected verdicts

checks.name: wire-ownership
checks.claim: one client owns the wire; a second is refused; preempt moves ownership and ends the previous client; release leaves no owner
checks.independence: observed behaviour against a local controller stub — one writer, one wire

checks.name: rotation-gate
checks.claim: a rotation changes the route only; it is refused unless both BAML paths agree on five fixtures, and refused when the binary is missing
checks.independence: self-referential: BAML vs BAML. Rules out a stale build, not a wrong lattice; the independent check is lattice-vs-reference
